patch.summary:
Choose Azure DevOps only if your buying job matches “Azure Repos/Boards/Pipelines — first 5 Basic users free, then $6/user/mo; Basic + Test Pla” rather than Bright Data's shape. Choose Bright Data only if your buying job matches “Web data / proxy platform — pay-as-you-go from ~$4/GB residential; starter commitments fro” rather than Azure DevOps's shape. Workflow advantage: Azure DevOps leans source-control-devops; Bright Data leans web-data-collection. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Azure DevOps is Azure Repos/Boards/Pipelines — first 5 Basic users free, then $6/user/mo; Basic + Test Plans $52/user/mo; Artifacts 2 GiB free.; Bright Data is Web data / proxy platform — pay-as-you-go from ~$4/GB residential; starter commitments from ~$499/mo..
- Workflow coverage skew: Azure DevOps-leaning source-control-devops vs Bright Data-leaning web-data-collection.
- Researched limits: Azure DevOps — User 6 onwards is $6/user/mo for every additional Basic seat — the free five are not a forever team cap workaround; Bright Data — GB/commitment pricing is opaque without live calculator — medium pricing confidence.

Limitations — Azure DevOps: User 6 onwards is $6/user/mo for every additional Basic seat — the free five are not a forever team cap workaround; Test Plans at $52/user is a QA licence, not something to assign to every developer; Bright Data: GB/commitment pricing is opaque without live calculator — medium pricing confidence; Compliance and acceptable-use rules must be validated per project.
